Exact proof reconstructed via companion-matrix congruences, factorization of the unit-power difference and finite-ball counts
correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the all-depth argument for d>=1, 5 not dividing d. In the binomial expansion of F_m/m the term indexed by j>=1 has a factor 5 after dividing by (2j+1)!, so the leading quotient on the four index classes is (2,1,3,4) modulo five (F_0 is treated separately). For the companion matrix Q, (F_21,F_20,F_19)=(10946,6765,4181) gives Q^20=I+5B mod 25 with B=((4,3),(3,1)); the (1,2) entries of Q^r B mod 5 for r=0,1,2,3 are (3,4,2,1), and Q^4 B=B mod 5. Binomial lifting gives exact difference valuation for indices in the same mod-four class, including index zero by the matrix or residue formula. On a fixed mod-four branch and input unit class u0 mod 5, the factor in (u^d-v^d)/(u-v) is a unit, so the normalized output map on each finite level bijects that ball with its leading-unit output ball. The CRT and the d-th-power map on F_5^* give respectively four or eight unit-branch preimages depending on 4|d; each has 5^((d-1)a) lifts, while the zero fiber consists exactly of multiples of 5^ceil(k/d). For period minimality the comparison at n=0 forces 5|T. At n=1 the mod-five quotients force 4|T for odd d or 2|T for even d; within those permitted classes the same isometry and 5 not dividing d force 5^k|T. These shifts are periods. The compatible shell images give the closure and the geometric-series Haar measure, including 5/6 and 125/312 at d=2 and d=4.
residual_risks: No extension to exponents divisible by five or to other primes is established. The supplied finite tests were not used as an all-depth proof.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the explicit classification of the power-index images and fibers for d>1, together with the transformed least periods and resulting closure. Ordinary Fibonacci equidistribution (and hence the d=1 case here) and the valuation rule are classical, and the five-adic analytic interpolation and general Haar-density method are also prior. The claim is an elementary development of those tools, not a new interpolation theory. No inspected theorem gives the full restricted classification.
residual_risks: An earlier implicit restricted-power classification could exist under a local analytic formulation. Interpolation is firmly established prior work; publication priority is not certified.

Classical ordinary-progressions and valuation statements as baseline
value.rationale: The tame family is defined by the natural nonsingularity condition for unit lifting. The problem asks which residue classes can be represented by a classical recurrence under nonlinear sampling, not just whether Fibonacci valuations take prescribed values. The change in allowable leading units and fiber size at 4|d and the even-exponent period halving distinguish actual effects of sampling; the formulas resolve the image and counting problem at every depth for the entire tame family.
residual_risks: The classification is local to five and does not claim a general theory of polynomial sampling or wild powers.
